findings.summary: The note under the std::ref example says the thread "gets a copy" without saying the example would fail to compile, so a learner may expect it to build and leave n at 0.
findings.evidence: void inc(int& n) { ++n; } ... std::thread t(inc, std::ref(n)); ... "without std::ref, the thread gets a copy"
findings.fix: Change the note to: "without std::ref the argument is copied, and for an int& parameter like this one it does not compile; a by-value parameter would compile and silently change only the copy."

findings.summary: Code snippet appears before the idea behind it is stated for std::ref, and a trailing remark is detached from the code.
findings.evidence:
cpp
void inc(int& n) { ++n; }
... t.join();  // n == 1
without std::ref, the thread gets a copy
findings.fix: State the one-line rule 'without std::ref the thread gets a copy' directly under the 'To pass a reference, wrap it in std::ref' bullet, then show the code.

findings.summary: The jthread cancel example is shown before the cancellation idea is stated, and the cooperative note trails the code.
findings.evidence:
cpp
std::jthread w([](std::stop_token st) {...});
w.request_stop();  // dtor then joins
cooperative: the thread must check the token
findings.fix: Put 'Cancellation is cooperative: the thread must check stop_token' before the code block.

findings.summary: The exceptions section has a bullet holding two alternatives, and the hand-off to the joiner is crammed into one bullet.
findings.evidence: Store std::current_exception() in an exception_ptr, then rethrow_exception in the joiner
findings.fix: Split into two bullets: 'Capture with std::current_exception() into an exception_ptr' and 'Joiner calls rethrow_exception'.

findings.summary: Code block mixes four unrelated idioms with no ideas stated first, and the mutex type of rw is only explained after the code.
findings.evidence:
std::scoped_lock lk(m1, m2);  // deadlock-safe
std::unique_lock u(m1, std::defer_lock);
std::shared_lock rd(rw);  // many readers
... rw is a std::shared_mutex
findings.fix: Split into two small blocks (multi-lock, reader/writer) each preceded by a one-line idea, and declare rw as std::shared_mutex in the snippet.

findings.summary: The wait/notify code is shown before the lost-wakeup and mutex rules are explained, and the first bullet packs several ideas.
findings.evidence: Always wait with a predicate: it handles spurious wakeups and lost notifications
findings.fix: Split into separate bullets for spurious wakeups and lost notifications.

findings.summary: The CAS example is shown before the doubling idea is explained, and the strong/weak bullets are scattered.
findings.fix: Add one line stating 'CAS: update only if the value is unchanged, else reload and retry' before the code.

findings.summary: The 'Ignored future' warning appears as a prose callout and is repeated on page 6, so the same point is stated twice.
findings.evidence: A future from async blocks in its destructor until the task ends. Discard it and the call is synchronous.
findings.fix: Keep one callout on the async page and have the cheat sheet use a single short row.

findings.summary: The promise example comes before the writer/reader idea, and one bullet combines set_value, set_exception and get_future.
findings.evidence: set_value or set_exception sets the result; get_future() is the reader side
findings.fix: State 'writer holds the promise, reader holds the future' first, then split the bullet into two.
